meta.name: Virtonomics
meta.refresh_cadence: quarterly — product-only benchmark, low expected rate of change; not worth a tighter cadence given thin public footprint

snapshot.one_liner: Massively multiplayer online business-simulation game (Cyprus studio Gamerflot; originally 'Money Mania' 2004, renamed Virtonomics 2006) where players run virtual companies across 200+ industries, competing against other players in real time.
snapshot.why_they_compete: Medium-high similarity: gamified business building for students and entrepreneurs, per COMPETITORS.md (#8 of 10); large in-game community claimed (~1M players).

positioning.value_prop: Markets itself as 'the most realistic business simulation game about company management and economics' / 'The #1 Economics Simulation Game in the World.' Three modes: Entrepreneur, Business War, Tycoon.
positioning.differentiation: A persistent, always-on multiplayer economy (vs. a bounded course-length simulation), spanning casual gaming to serious economic-strategy/PvP play.

1_identity.audience_icp: Broad: business students/educators, aspiring entrepreneurs, business professionals, strategy-game hobbyists; also corporate/school 'Business Challenge' competitions.

similarity_to_us.rationale: Strong gamification match, but the persistent-multiplayer/PvP-economy format and broad hobbyist audience diverge from Altitut's structured, cohort-based education model. Directional judgment, not a scoring model.

highlight_features.why_pushed: The core differentiator — an always-on shared world rather than a bounded simulation.

highlight_features.feature: Three play modes (Entrepreneur, Business War, Tycoon)
highlight_features.why_pushed: Segments casual learners from competitive/serious players.

most_attractive_features.why_it_lands: Creates long-term retention/community that outlives a single course or cohort, unlike bounded classroom simulations.

messaging_conversion.headline_copy: not available — not captured in this desk-research pass
messaging_conversion.pricing: Free-to-play / freemium (explicitly marketed as a 'Free business game'); premium features implied but not detailed on-site.
messaging_conversion.social_proof: User-base claims found only in press, not verified current: ~1 million registered users claimed in a 2015 PR release, 'exceeding 2 million' by 2018 sources, and current site language vaguely references 'millions of our users' — treat as unverified marketing claims, not confirmed active-player counts.

insights_to_imbibe: The persistent, always-on multiplayer economy creates long-term retention/community — Altitut's RPG framing could borrow a persistent shared 'world' or leaderboard layer that outlives a single course or cohort.

8_synthesis.winning_formula: A free-to-play, persistent multiplayer business simulation sustained by long-term player retention rather than course-length engagement.

steal: A persistent, shared multiplayer world/leaderboard layer that outlives individual courses or cohorts.
